# 2. Technologies Worth Watching

**Technology:** Scoped, short-lived credentials for agents (e.g., Vercel Connect)

**Category:** AI / Security / Cloud

**What happened?**
Vercel announced (Jun 17, London) a layer that gives agents temporary, scoped credentials for external tools, alongside longer function runtimes (30 min) and 24-hour sandboxes. Source is a press release syndicated on a regional news site; unverified by us.

**Why it matters?**
It validates one concrete rule for our standard: no agent holds a long-lived secret. Credential scope and expiry are enforceable controls, unlike "be careful".

**Business Value:** Smaller blast radius if an agent or connector is compromised; easier audit answers.

**Company Relevance:** 65

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Observe (adopt the principle in the standard now; evaluate products only if we deploy on that platform)

**Expected Impact:** Medium

# 4. Global Technology Direction

**Where is the market moving?**

- **Agents are becoming the unit of deployment.** Platform vendors (Vercel's framing: agents as the dominant way software gets deployed) are building runtime, identity and credential layers, not just models.
- **Money follows risk.** Security and governance for agents is a funded category; expect many small vendors and consolidation. Buy principles now, products later.
- **Quiet news weeks continue.** After the September model wave, the gap between announcements and usable, priced APIs is the real constraint.

**Strategic implications:** Control-plane design (identity, scope, spend, logs) will outlast any single model choice. Teams with a written standard can adopt any of these products quickly; teams without one cannot evaluate them.

## What This Means For Our Company

1. Add "short-lived, scoped credentials only" to the draft agent-control standard.
2. Do not buy agent security products before the standard exists; we cannot specify requirements yet.
3. Cost-model refresh and eval set remain the right next measurements.
